## SEO Services Singapore: Agency vs In-house vs S$20/month
URL: https://pageonesingapore.com/seo-services-singapore/
Last updated: 2026-10-17

Comparing SEO services in Singapore? Agency retainers, hiring an SEO executive or Page One at S$20/month: typical costs, what you get and when each makes sense.

Q: How much do SEO services cost in Singapore?
A: It varies a lot by provider and scope. As a general guide, small business SEO retainers from agencies are often somewhere around S$500 to S$3,000 or more a month, sometimes with a setup or audit fee. Hiring an in-house SEO or digital marketing executive typically means a salary of roughly S$3,000 to S$5,000 a month plus employer CPF and tools. These are typical ranges, not quotes. Page One's Get Found plan is S$20 a month (introductory price), with optional SEO Boosts at S$10 each, no setup fee and no contract.

Q: Is an SEO agency better than Page One?
A: It depends on what you need. An agency can make sense if you have a larger budget, compete for national searches, sell in several markets or want ads and SEO handled together. Page One is built for new and small local businesses that want the essentials done properly at a low monthly cost: a website, Google and Google Maps setup, AI search setup, regular articles and a monthly technical audit.

Q: Should I hire an in-house SEO executive or outsource?
A: Hire if you have enough marketing work to keep a full-time person busy, for example social media, ads, content and events as well as SEO. If what you mainly need is for your website to be found on Google and Google Maps, outsourcing the SEO groundwork usually costs far less, and you can still hire later when there's more to do.

Q: How much does it cost to hire an SEO or digital marketing executive in Singapore?
A: Salaries for these roles typically range from around S$3,000 to S$5,000 a month depending on experience, as a general guide. On top of salary, employers pay CPF of 17% for Singapore citizens and PRs aged 55 and below, plus paid SEO tools, leave cover, training and your own time managing the role. For example, a S$3,500 salary plus 17% CPF is about S$4,095 a month before tools or bonus.

Q: What does Page One not do?
A: We don't run paid ads, manage your social media accounts, or buy links. We don't promise rankings, because no honest provider can. We focus on organic (unpaid) visibility on Google, Google Maps and AI assistants like ChatGPT for local small businesses.

Q: Can Page One work alongside my marketing executive?
A: Yes. We look after the website and the Google and AI search groundwork, and your executive can send us updates on WhatsApp while they focus on social media, ads and customers.

Q: Do you guarantee page one on Google?
A: No. Google decides rankings, so no honest provider can guarantee them. Be careful of anyone who does. We document the work instead, and you can see your own numbers in Google Search Console.

Q: Is there a contract or setup fee?
A: No. The Get Found plan is S$20 a month at an introductory price, paid monthly in advance, with no setup fee and no minimum contract. Cancel anytime by WhatsApp.

Q: How do I check that an SEO company in Singapore is legitimate?
A: Look the company up on ACRA's Bizfile by name or UEN, ask for Google Search Console numbers with the date range shown for a website you can visit, open the client websites they name, and read the minimum term in the contract. Be careful with headline promises like "Rank #1" that their own small print says no one can guarantee. Page One's company details, client websites and dated Search Console results are all published so you can check them.

## Fully Managed Website Singapore: S$20/month, All-In
URL: https://pageonesingapore.com/managed-website-singapore/
Last updated: 2026-10-14

A fully managed website for your Singapore business: design, hosting, security, SEO articles, AEO and GEO, all for S$20/month. No setup fee or contract.

Q: What does a fully managed website mean?
A: It means you don't have to touch the technical side at all. Page One builds the website on your own domain, hosts it, keeps it online, secure and fast, runs a technical audit every month, makes small text and photo changes when you WhatsApp us, and keeps publishing new articles so Google and AI assistants have reasons to show you. All of it is in the S$20 a month plan.

Q: What is AEO (answer engine optimisation)?
A: AEO means setting up your pages so that when someone asks a question, Google's AI answers or ChatGPT can use your page as the answer. In practice that means clear question-and-answer content, FAQ structured data, and your business details written plainly, which we do for every site.

Q: What is GEO (generative engine optimisation)?
A: GEO means helping AI tools that write answers, such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity, find, read and correctly describe your business. We connect your site to Google and Bing, mark up your business details with structured data, publish an llms.txt summary and keep your details the same everywhere. No one can guarantee an AI tool will recommend you, but these steps make it possible.

Q: What is not included in the S$20?
A: Your domain name, which is registered in your name and paid to the registrar directly, usually S$15–30 a year. SEO Boosts are optional at S$10 each, for when you want more articles aimed at new keywords. There is no setup fee and no contract.

Q: Will the S$20 price go up?
A: S$20 a month is an introductory price until we reach our early-client target. When it goes up, the new price will stay close to S$20.

Q: Who owns the website and the domain?
A: Your domain is registered in your name, so you always own it. If you cancel, your site stays live until the end of the month you paid for, you keep your domain, and you can buy the site files if you want to host them elsewhere.

Q: How long until my website is live?
A: Usually within 7 days of receiving your details and photos. You send them over WhatsApp, and we do the rest.

Q: Is S$20 a month too cheap to be any good?
A: The price is low because AI now does the daily work that used to be billed by the hour, not because steps are skipped. Edwin Garage got 2,275 clicks from Google in the 28 days to 13 October 2026, according to Google Search Console, and every client website is live for you to check.

## SEO, AEO and GEO Singapore: All Three from S$20/month
URL: https://pageonesingapore.com/seo-aeo-geo-singapore/
Last updated: 2026-10-15

SEO for Google, AEO for Google's answers and AI Overviews, GEO for ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity: what each means and how we do all three for S$20/month.

Q: What is AEO (answer engine optimisation)?
A: AEO, answer engine optimisation, means shaping your pages so Google can lift a short answer straight from them into a featured snippet, a People Also Ask box or an AI Overview. We do it by putting customers' real questions in headings and answering each one in two or three plain sentences, marked up with FAQ structured data.

Q: What is GEO (generative engine optimisation)?
A: GEO, generative engine optimisation, means helping AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini, Perplexity and Copilot find your business, describe it correctly and name it as a source. We publish clear business facts and an llms.txt summary, allow AI crawlers in robots.txt, connect your site to Bing and Google, and keep your details consistent. No one can guarantee a mention.

Q: Do I need SEO, AEO and GEO?
A: Most small businesses benefit from all three, because customers now look in three places: Google's results, the answers Google shows above them, and AI assistants. The three share the same groundwork, so doing them together costs less than doing them separately. With Page One, all three are part of the S$20 a month plan, with no setup fee.

Q: How do I know it's working?
A: Google Search Console is connected to your site from day one, so you can see how often you appear on Google, what people searched and how many clicked. AI assistants have no official report yet, so the simplest check is to ask ChatGPT or Perplexity about your type of business in your area and see who is named.

## AI SEO vs Traditional SEO: Cheap, Not Low Quality | Page One
URL: https://pageonesingapore.com/ai-seo-vs-traditional-seo/
Last updated: 2026-10-14

Why AI-powered SEO costs less than traditional, labour-based SEO without cutting quality. A side-by-side comparison, GEO for AI search, and real Google results.

Q: What is the difference between AI SEO and traditional SEO?
A: The goal is the same: help a business show up when customers search. The difference is how the work gets done. Traditional SEO is mostly done by hand, so it's priced by the hours people spend on it. Page One uses AI and automation for the repetitive daily work, such as checking pages, reading Search Console data, writing articles and telling Google and Bing about changes. Edwin designs the strategy and the system and reviews the results.

Q: Why is Page One so cheap?
A: Because most of the cost of SEO has always been people's time, and AI now does most of the routine work. The Get Found plan is S$20 a month (introductory price) because fewer hours are needed, not because steps are skipped. The same system runs Edwin Garage, Edwin's own workshop, which got 2,275 clicks from Google in the 28 days to 13 October 2026, according to Google Search Console.

Q: Is automated SEO low quality?
A: Quality comes from the strategy, the site structure and what gets published, not from how many hours were billed. The results are measurable: in the 28 days to 13 October 2026, Edwin Garage appeared on page one of Google for more than 4,290 different searches and Cleanic Detailing for 1,226, according to Google Search Console. We follow Google's guidelines: no bought links, no fake reviews and no keyword stuffing.

Q: Is AI SEO weaker than an expensive agency?
A: No. An agency's edge is its analysis of the competition: studying the pages Google already ranks and building something better. Page One's EDGE Loop does the same analysis, then keeps watching your Search Console data every day instead of once a month. The cost is lower because the repetitive work is automated, not because steps are skipped.

Q: What is GEO (generative engine optimisation)?
A: GEO means making a business easy for AI assistants such as ChatGPT, Gemini and Perplexity to read, understand and mention. Page One does this with structured data (Schema.org), an llms.txt summary, Bing Webmaster Tools (Bing powers ChatGPT search) and content that answers customers' questions clearly. No one can guarantee an AI assistant will recommend a business, but these steps make it possible.

Q: Does the system really work around the clock?
A: It runs on a schedule, every day, including weekends and public holidays. Google Search Console data is pulled in automatically, and new articles are picked from the searches Google already shows a site for. When something needs a person, it is flagged to Edwin.

Q: Does a person still look after my site?
A: Yes. Edwin designs the strategy and the system, reviews the results and replies on WhatsApp personally. Automation does the legwork. It doesn't replace judgement.

Q: Can you guarantee page one rankings?
A: No, and no honest provider can, because Google decides rankings. What we can show you is the same system working on real Singapore businesses, with dated Google Search Console data, and a report for every SEO Boost.

Q: When is traditional SEO the better choice?
A: When you need more than search groundwork: paid ads managed for you, a large online shop with thousands of products, several countries, or a big link-building and PR campaign. An agency or an in-house team is the better fit there.

## Google Ads vs SEO vs AI Blog Tools in Singapore | Page One
URL: https://pageonesingapore.com/google-ads-vs-seo-vs-ai-blog-tools/
Last updated: 2026-10-17

Google Ads, AI blog autopilot tools or a done-for-you website with SEO? What each includes, what it costs, where each fits, with a side-by-side table.

Q: Is SEO cheaper than Google Ads?
A: Usually, over time. With Google Ads you pay for every click, so the cost grows with the traffic and stops when you stop paying. SEO is a fixed monthly cost for the work, and the unpaid clicks it earns cost nothing each. Page One's SEO is S$20 a month, but results build gradually and no one can guarantee rankings.

Q: Do AI blog tools build my website?
A: Most don't. An AI blog autopilot tool usually needs a website you already have, and it adds articles to it. Hosting, security, page speed, your Google Business Profile and Search Console are normally left to you. Page One includes the website, hosting and that setup in the S$20 a month, with the articles.

Q: Does Page One run Google Ads for me?
A: No. Page One focuses on organic, unpaid visibility on Google Search, Google Maps and AI assistants like ChatGPT. We don't run paid ads, manage social media or buy links. If you want ads managed, an agency or a Google Ads specialist is the better fit, and your Page One website can still be the page your ads link to.

Q: How fast does each one work?
A: Google Ads can show as soon as a campaign is approved and funded. SEO usually takes weeks to months, because Google has to find, trust and rank your pages. AI blog tools add articles quickly, but each article still has to earn its place. Page One sites are usually live within 7 days of getting your details.

Q: Are AI-written articles bad for SEO?
A: Not by themselves. Google says it rewards helpful content however it is produced, but mass-produced pages made mainly to rank break its spam policies. What matters is that each article answers a real customer question accurately. Page One picks article topics from your own Search Console data, so each one answers a search your customers really make.

Q: Can I cancel Page One anytime?
A: Yes. There is no setup fee and no contract, so you can cancel anytime. The only other cost is your domain name, which is registered in your name and paid by you directly, usually S$15 to S$30 a year. Optional SEO Boosts are S$10 each, and you choose whether to buy any.
